clusters.headline: Soft-deprecating re.match()

items.title: Soft-deprecating re.match()
items.extract: Soft-deprecating re.match() Python has a concept of soft deprecation , where APIs are marked as "should no longer be used to write new code" without any promise/threat to remove them in the future. Python 3.15 release manager Hugo van Kemenade describes how in the upcoming 3.15 release soft deprecation has come for the venerable but deeply confusing re.match() function. It's now available with the much clearer alternative re.prefixmatch() name - reflecting how it anchors at the beginning of the string but not the end. Most of the time you probably want re.search() (match this pattern anywhere in the string) or re.fullmatch() (match the entire string) instead.

clusters.summary: Python 3.15 release manager Hugo van Kemenade has announced the soft deprecation of the re.match() function. Under this soft deprecation status, the API is designated as no longer recommended for new code without any plans for future removal. The function is now supplemented by the clearer alternative re.prefixmatch(), which indicates that it anchors only at the beginning of a string rather than the end.

clusters.headline: GPU-CFR: 80x Faster Counterfactual Regret Minimization by Compiling the Game to Static Dataflow and CUDA Graph Replay

items.title: GPU-CFR: 80x Faster Counterfactual Regret Minimization by Compiling the Game to Static Dataflow and CUDA Graph Replay
items.extract: Counterfactual regret minimization (CFR) is one of the few large numerical workloads that still runs faster on CPUs than on GPUs. Each iteration sweeps a game tree with up to billions of states in millions of small, interdependent gather and scatter steps issued through a generic tree interface. On a GPU every kernel finishes in microseconds, so kernel launches and framework dispatch dominate the run time, and prior GPU implementations have lost to optimized CPU code. We observe that for a fixed game, everything about a CFR iteration except the numerical values is known before the first iteration runs. We propose GPU-CFR, a compiler and runtime built on this observation.

clusters.summary: GPU-CFR achieves an 80x speedup in counterfactual regret minimization by compiling games to static dataflow and utilizing CUDA graph replay. Counterfactual regret minimization traditionally runs faster on CPUs than on GPUs because small, interdependent gather and scatter steps across billions of game tree states cause kernel launches and framework dispatch to dominate GPU runtimes. To overcome this, GPU-CFR leverages the insight that all aspects of a CFR iteration except the numerical values are known prior to the first iteration for a fixed game.

clusters.headline: From Protocols to Evidence: Bounded Claims for AI in Service of the Common Good

items.title: From Protocols to Evidence: Bounded Claims for AI in Service of the Common Good
items.extract: Artificial Intelligence does more than create a governance problem. It can also reveal where institutions have already failed to provide responsiveness, belonging, care, and accountability. Once deployed, AI becomes an intervention in those conditions. It can repair, compound, substitute for, or conceal the failures it encounters. Responsible AI must therefore evaluate both the system and the institutional rupture into which it is introduced. The move from principles to protocols is already underway. The EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, and assurance practices translate commitments into roles, requirements, records, oversight, and assessment.

clusters.summary: Artificial Intelligence acts as an intervention that can repair, compound, substitute for, or conceal institutional failures related to responsiveness, belonging, care, and accountability. Consequently, responsible artificial intelligence requires evaluating both the system itself and the specific institutional rupture where it is introduced. The ongoing transition from principles to protocols involves frameworks like the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, and assurance practices. These mechanisms translate high-level commitments into concrete roles, requirements, records, oversight, and assessment.

clusters.headline: Ex-Deepmind VP Vinyals says AI self-improvement is coming but won't trigger an intelligence explosion

items.title: Ex-Deepmind VP Vinyals says AI self-improvement is coming but won't trigger an intelligence explosion
items.extract: Oriol Vinyals, until recently head of research at Google DeepMind, thinks a sudden AI intelligence explosion through recursive self-improvement is unlikely. AI can speed up research by a factor of ten, he says, but it hits two bottlenecks: coming up with ideas ("research taste") and reliably judging results. Reward hacking and the speed of light add further limits. Vinyals now wants to tackle these bottlenecks with his startup Discovery Loop, co-founded with Jeff Dean, Sanjay Ghemawat, and Quoc Le.

clusters.summary: Former Google DeepMind research head Oriol Vinyals argues that while artificial intelligence recursive self-improvement is approaching, it will not cause an abrupt intelligence explosion. Vinyals notes that although AI can accelerate research tenfold, it faces obstacles including "research taste," reliable evaluation of outcomes, reward hacking, and physical speed-of-light limits. To address these hurdles, Vinyals has launched the startup Discovery Loop alongside co-founders Jeff Dean, Sanjay Ghemawat, and Quoc Le.

clusters.headline: Deep learning pioneer Bengio argues the training process itself makes AI dangerous

items.title: Deep learning pioneer Bengio argues the training process itself makes AI dangerous
items.extract: AI pioneer Yoshua Bengio warns in a new essay that AI agents could learn to deceive, game rules, and hide bad behavior as they get better at optimizing goals. He calls for independent safety reviews before any further training or deployment. US President Trump disagrees and wants to keep outpacing China in the AI race.

clusters.summary: Deep learning pioneer Yoshua Bengio asserts in a recent essay that the training process itself makes artificial intelligence dangerous because optimizing goals could cause AI agents to learn deception, rule-gaming, and the concealment of bad behavior. To mitigate these risks, Bengio demands independent safety reviews prior to conducting any additional training or deployment. Meanwhile, US President Trump rejects this perspective and aims to maintain the lead over China in the artificial intelligence competition.

clusters.headline: How hackers used Claude for missiles, drone swarms, and surveillance, while Chinese labs mined it for training data

items.title: How hackers used Claude for missiles, drone swarms, and surveillance, while Chinese labs mined it for training data
items.extract: Anthropic's new threat intelligence report documents eight months of Claude abuse. Chinese AI labs like Alibaba's Qwen team, DeepSeek, and Moonshot AI relayed requests en masse or extracted training data, with Qwen alone accounting for more than 151 million exchanges. Actors also used Claude for missile software, autonomous kamikaze drones, and nationwide surveillance systems.

clusters.summary: Anthropic released a new threat intelligence report documenting eight months of Claude abuse by malicious actors and Chinese AI labs. Alibaba's Qwen team, DeepSeek, and Moonshot AI extracted training data or relayed requests en masse, with Qwen alone responsible for over 151 million exchanges. Additionally, actors leveraged Claude to develop missile software, autonomous kamikaze drones, and nationwide surveillance systems.

clusters.headline: Y Combinator’s Garry Tan wants US open-weight AI labs to ‘distill’ frontier models, too

items.title: Y Combinator’s Garry Tan wants US open-weight AI labs to ‘distill’ frontier models, too
items.extract: Tan wants smaller, American open-weight AI labs to use the same kind of training techniques on American frontier AI labs, giving the U.S. a more robust set of open-weight options that aren’t Chinese.

clusters.summary: Y Combinator leader Garry Tan is calling on domestic open-weight artificial intelligence laboratories to distill frontier artificial intelligence models. This initiative aims to provide the United States with a stronger variety of open-weight alternatives originating outside of China. Under this proposal, smaller American open-weight labs would apply identical training methods used on leading U.S. frontier artificial intelligence models.
